headline: Red Sox offense flatlines as Patriots break our hearts again
morning_brew: Another night at the oldest yard in baseball, another result that leaves me staring at the ceiling in the dark. That four to six loss to the Angels was a gut-punch, especially watching the bats struggle to find any daylight until it was far too late. We put eight hits on the board, but they arrived in useless little pieces rather than the kind of sustained pressure that puts a crooked number on the scoreboard. It feels like we are spinning our wheels in the stretch run, and at this point I am watching these games the way you watch a slow-motion car crash. You know exactly what is coming, but you cannot look away.

Switching gears to the gridiron, that season opener in Seattle was a absolute heartbreaker. Dropping a ten to thirteen decision after leading at halftime is the kind of stuff that makes you question why we put ourselves through this every autumn. Drake Maye had a rough go with those three interceptions, and frankly, we need more efficiency if we want to compete in a league this unforgiving. I have always been one to preach patience, but seeing the offense sputter in the fourth quarter when a drive was there for the taking just hurts, plain and simple.

With no game today, I am planning on taking a breather to let the frustration of both losses subside. My neighbor Rick has been pacing his driveway for an hour, convinced that the officiating crews are conspiring against Boston across all sports, but I think the issues are much closer to home. We get back to the Fens on Thursday night against Kansas City, and I will be sitting in my usual spot hoping for a clean, professional effort. We are still in the mix for the postseason, so let's hope the team finds their rhythm before the window slams shut.
